a.disclosed: Popover contains the existing inclusion callback choices and duration/diagnostic links; Detalles holds all task properties; options remain scoped.
a.access: 44px trigger and choices, native radio semantics, Escape and focus return; no hover dependency.
a.benefit: Clarifies the consequence of adding routines before changing scope.
a.risk: A preview must use existing summaries without inventing totals.
a.verification: Switch page and section scope independently; compare displayed contributions, history dates and selection after closing.

b.title: Heading-first spoken outline
b.mechanism: From first principles, screen-reader navigation should mirror the real hierarchy: page h1 with period description, section h2 with scope description, tasks as labelled list items. Visually replace badges with quiet description lines.
b.visible: Clear heading outline, completion and one contextual secondary line.
b.disclosed: Details regions retain metadata edits and links; summary regions retain estimates and diagnostics; all options have explicit scoped labels.
b.access: 44px controls, aria-labelledby/ describedby relationships and decorative icons hidden; focus visible.
b.benefit: Makes structural navigation dependable while reducing isolated visual symbols.
b.risk: Overlong descriptions could become repetitive speech.
b.verification: Inspect heading order, descriptions for historical periods, completed task state and every property action through keyboard navigation.

a.title: Ancestor summary transfer
a.mechanism: A nested user inverts repeated hierarchy summaries by placing aggregate duration/count in the highest expanded ancestor and showing descendant summaries only through Details. Each descendant retains its own name, scope exception and Options route; task metadata is likewise disclosed.
a.visible: Ancestor totals, descendant titles, scope differences, selected date and completion.
a.disclosed: Details returns every descendant estimate and breakdown, inclusion control and metadata editor; Options preserves existing commands. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px named targets; accessible descriptions state aggregate scope; no altered calculations.
a.benefit: Removes repeated totals while preserving ownership cues.
a.risk: Aggregate totals may be misread as own-section totals.
a.verification: Verify no double counting changes, parent/child labels, collapse transitions, duration and mobile menus.

b.title: Unified glass context capsule
b.mechanism: For minimal users under constraints, consolidate related header navigation into one restrained glass capsule with period label, scope label and disclosure; sections/tasks stay opaque, flat and compact.
b.visible: Header period/scope, section count/title, task title/check and date exceptions.
b.disclosed: Capsule opens grouped period, inclusion, estimates and diagnostic controls; section/task Details and Options preserve existing editors, links, menus and callbacks.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: One material boundary signals navigation without decorating every fact.
b.risk: A unified control could blur scope if its labels are vague.
b.verification: Verify capsule groups reference dates and full-routine state explicitly; inspect light/dark contrast and 320px wrapping.

a.title: Duration selection gutter
a.mechanism: For duration decisions, inversion asks what prevents comparing time before starting. Reserve a narrow numeric gutter for task active estimates, aligned with header total and section estimates; remove competing metadata from that gutter.
a.visible: Title, completion, active minutes, date exceptions and section subtotal.
a.disclosed: The gutter button opens existing duration editing and own/subtask/parallel breakdown; named Details and scope controls retain remaining metadata, routine inclusion and options.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: A single visual column supports comparison without badge clutter.
a.risk: Long duration formats could squeeze titles.
a.verification: Compare own plus nested subtask durations, parallel time and shopping exceptions at 320px.

b.title: One calm context tray
b.mechanism: For a busy caregiver, constraint-first disclosure reserves one glass navigation tray for date, routine scope and Details. MainPageHeader removes separate switches into this tray; section headers mirror its summary and task rows use a Details button.
b.visible: Title, selected period, scope label, completion and essential deadline.
b.disclosed: Tray expands existing period navigator, accumulated switch, duration breakdown and diagnostic; list and section options retain named routes; task panel contains all metadata editors. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px buttons, semantic expansion, restored focus; keyboard access and opaque glass fallback.
b.benefit: A single stable place carries supporting information.
b.risk: Combining scope and date could imply they share state.
b.verification: Check independent scope/date callbacks, duration, menus, completion and 320/375px.

a.title: Historical evidence sheet
a.mechanism: Constraint-first historical disclosure uses one Evidence sheet with tabs for Period, Routine and Estimates, opened from header/section Details. Task Details opens full original metadata with the same selected-period caption. Navigation alone receives glass.
a.visible: Historical period caption, scope, titles, counts, completion and Details.
a.disclosed: Sheet retains navigator, diagnostic, accumulated controls and duration splits; Options preserves commands; task editors and links keep original callbacks. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px tab/buttons, semantic tabs, focus trap/return, opaque fallback and reduced motion.
a.benefit: Several historical signals become one inspectable supporting surface.
a.risk: Tabs can hide cross-category relationships.
a.verification: Verify period persists across tabs, own/accumulated totals, focused editors, completion and mobile fit.

b.title: Recurrence route selectors
b.mechanism: For mixed recurrence lists, adversarially prevent a scope switch from feeling like completion or filtering by date. Give page and section recurrence scope a dedicated labeled selector, while tasks show their own frequency beside Details.
b.visible: Selected inclusion scope, period, task frequency/title/check.
b.disclosed: Selector opens original only-section/full-routine action with explanatory count composition; task frequency invokes existing picker; estimates, diagnostic and all menus remain named.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Scope changes are visible and distinct from task recurrence editing.
b.risk: Two related recurrence controls may still require careful wording.
b.verification: Test page versus section callbacks, mixed frequencies, no recurrence and historical completion.

a.title: Recurrence inheritance sentence
a.mechanism: For mixed lists, first principles explains only information that cannot be inferred. Header says selected scope; section says included frequencies; task frequency appears only when differing from its section, with explicit Mixed label where needed.
a.visible: Inherited section recurrence, differing task frequency, date/check/title and period.
a.disclosed: Details shows every task's full recurrence and original picker even when inherited; estimates, count breakdown, routine toggle, diagnostic and options remain accessible.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: Reduces repetitive recurrence text while keeping exceptions obvious.
a.risk: Incorrect inheritance could misrepresent manually assigned cycles.
a.verification: Test computed periodicity from list, section, title and cycle, including custom cycles.

b.title: History margin notes
b.mechanism: The historical reviewer inverts current-date assumptions through margin notes: header gives selected period, section captions give period-specific status, and task notes expose differing due dates. All decorative capsules become plain text; complete metadata is disclosed.
b.visible: Selected period, section context status, differing due dates, titles and completion.
b.disclosed: Context-note buttons open navigator/diagnostic and duration; task Details retains every editor and link; named Options retains management and inclusion. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px note hit areas, noncolor date cues, wrapping text and restored focus.
b.benefit: Period-specific explanations remain visible during historical scanning.
b.risk: Margin layout may require stacking at small widths.
b.verification: Verify rollover labels use referenceDate, past mixed frequencies, all-done/partial states and 320/375px.

a.title: Two separate disclosures
a.mechanism: The organizer's adversarial disclosure separates information from commands: every page, section and task has a Details route and an Options route, eliminating ambiguity over whether summaries change state. Keep completion outside both.
a.visible: Titles, selected period, count, completion, Details and Options.
a.disclosed: Details show full duration, accumulated breakdown and all metadata editors; Options retain existing list/section/task command menus and scope toggles with current state. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: Each route is 44px, visibly labeled, keyboard operable and focus-restoring.
a.benefit: Users can inspect shared work without accidentally invoking commands.
a.risk: Two routes may still occupy considerable width.
a.verification: Test no metadata opener completes a task, every original command remains reachable and 320px layout stacks.

b.title: One open time calculator
b.mechanism: For duration decisions, adversarially test a task whose quiet estimate hides substantial subtask time. Allow one inline duration disclosure per scope, replacing badges with a labeled Time button that expands a complete breakdown.
b.visible: Header total and period, section count, task title, Time value.
b.disclosed: Expanded calculator shows own/subtask active time, parallel time and edit-duration action; adjacent Details preserves date, frequency, price and navigation; scope/options remain named.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Comparison stays available while detail occupies space only when requested.
b.risk: Opening another calculator can close needed comparison context.
b.verification: Test opening via keyboard, switching rows without completing tasks and inherited plus parallel estimates.

a.title: Focusable side inspector
a.mechanism: Under keyboard constraints, use a persistent inspector on desktop opened by page, section or task Inspeccionar controls; mobile uses the same content in a sheet. Headers become compact and tasks retain completion.
a.visible: Identity, period, scope summary and completion.
a.disclosed: Inspector shows all object-specific facts and existing actions, including diagnostic, estimates, section menus and metadata editor shortcuts.
a.access: 44px inspectors; labelled panel, explicit close, predictable focus return; no focus-triggered automatic opening.
a.benefit: Avoids shifting the list whenever a keyboard user inspects properties.
a.risk: Desktop panel reduces available task width.
a.verification: Test selected object changes, deleted task focus fallback, mobile sheet trapping and every metadata action.

b.title: Magnifiable information panel
b.mechanism: Invert low-vision overload by opening all secondary facts in a generous information panel with larger text, explicit labels and full-width edit buttons. Page and section rows contain one named inspect route; tasks retain completion/title.
b.visible: Period and scope, titles, completion and large Inspectar controls.
b.disclosed: Panel retains all exact counts, estimates, metadata, diagnostic and option links appropriate to the chosen object.
b.access: 44px actions, scrollable labelled panel, focus management and minimum contrast; no decorative nested glass.
b.benefit: Makes dense facts readable without increasing every task's visual load.
b.risk: Inspecting different objects requires additional navigation.
b.verification: Open panel from task/section/page, test zoom and focus return, then verify all existing property edit callbacks.

a.title: Maintenance action itinerary
a.mechanism: A maintenance planner's first-principles action view makes existing Start sequence the anchor of a section itinerary. Header shows selected month; sections show ordered tasks and a final Start/Details footer; task completion remains individually available.
a.visible: Month, scope, section title/count, task titles and completion.
a.disclosed: Itinerary footer opens estimates, accumulated breakdown and Start; Options preserves management; task Details preserves every metadata action. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px controls, list order remains unchanged, semantic footer and restored focus.
a.benefit: Planning and execution connect to the exact section.
a.risk: Footers below long sections can be missed.
a.verification: Verify global and section Start scope, duration, ordering, keyboard routes and narrow overflow.

b.title: Deadline action row
b.mechanism: For urgent deadlines, adversarially protect against accidental completion from metadata taps. Separate each task into a completion/title row and a labeled deadline button row; header date and section period context remain fixed while summaries disclose.
b.visible: Completion target, title, urgent deadline in words, selected period and scope.
b.disclosed: Deadline button invokes date editing; Details provides all other task actions; header Estimates/Options and section Scope/Options retain totals, diagnostics and commands.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Urgency is actionable and visually distinct from finishing the task.
b.risk: Two-row tasks use more vertical space.
b.verification: Test touching deadline versus checkbox, past-period overdue context and keyboard focus order.

a.title: Sticky active-section context
a.mechanism: From first principles, a one-handed user needs the current section's context near current tasks. A restrained sticky section header keeps name, summary and options visible; global period remains in the top rail.
a.visible: Current section heading, small scope/count summary, selected period and completion.
a.disclosed: Section summary opens estimates/inclusion; page summary and task details retain full data and actions.
a.access: 44px sticky controls, bounded z-index, semantic headings and scroll margin for focused elements; no decorative blur on content.
a.benefit: Keeps section operations reachable after scrolling without repeating metadata on tasks.
a.risk: Stacked nested sticky headings can cover content.
a.verification: Test nested section depths, focus scrolling, existing drag/drop menus, 320px height and historical context labels.

b.title: Visible commitment ribbon
b.mechanism: For users needing visible reminders, constraint-first preserves deadline and recurrence as an explicit ribbon under task titles; header/section ribbons display their current period and accumulated scope using plain words.
b.visible: Title/check, deadline/recurrence ribbon, scope and section count.
b.disclosed: One Estimates button reveals durations/breakdowns; task Details retains all editors, time-of-day cycling, prices and links; page/section menus and diagnostic remain labeled.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Required reminders remain visibly present while ornamental metadata recedes.
b.risk: Ribbon repetition can still be busy in routine-heavy lists.
b.verification: Check recurring tasks without dates, historical references, rollover context and unchanged completion semantics.

a.title: Parallel lane pair
a.mechanism: For parallel-task planning, constraint-first separates active effort from concurrent effort without changing calculations. Header and section summaries use two labeled lanes; task metadata follows the same active/parallel pair inside a flat row, with glass reserved for navigation.
a.visible: Active minutes, parallel minutes when present, period, scope and completion.
a.disclosed: Lane headings expose existing breakdowns; Details contains duration editing and other metadata; each section has a dedicated menu and inclusion control.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: Parallel work remains distinguishable without repeated lightning badges.
a.risk: Users may mistakenly add the lanes into elapsed time.
a.verification: Test parallel-only, mixed and subtask estimates; verify lane wording makes no elapsed-time claim.

b.title: Household ledger
b.mechanism: A first-principles household view uses an aligned ledger: page header is a caption, section headers are ledger dividers, task rows share a title column and one quiet context column. At mobile width the context column becomes a disclosed line.
b.visible: Caption with period, section count, completion and a concise deadline or context value.
b.disclosed: A Context button expands complete metadata; summary footer opens duration and routine diagnostics; named menus preserve all commands and scope settings. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px controls, semantic lists, tabular counters and readable opaque rows.
b.benefit: Shared alignment replaces many independent badge shapes.
b.risk: Fixed columns can squeeze long household titles.
b.verification: Verify long titles, nested rows, price/duration totals, historical reference dates and desktop/mobile conversion.

a.title: Stable essential spine
a.mechanism: For minimal users, adversarially test quiet UI with keyboard and screen reader. Maintain an identical visible spine: scope heading, selected period, task checkbox/title, named Details, named Options; metadata appears inline only after explicit disclosure.
a.visible: Essential spine and nonredundant date exceptions; inclusion state always stated.
a.disclosed: Details expands semantic definition lists containing every datum and original action; header/section summaries use the same disclosure pattern, with diagnostic and inclusion controls retained.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: Predictable focus structure keeps minimalism operable.
a.risk: Many Details buttons need object-specific accessible names.
a.verification: Verify tab order, expanded state, focus ring, all commands and no invisible focus targets.

b.title: Breadcrumb context rail
b.mechanism: Invert keyboard disorientation by showing a textual context rail: list, selected period, routine scope. Each segment is a separate labelled control; sections add their local scope underneath and tasks suppress inherited repetition.
b.visible: Context rail and task completion; section headings remain semantic.
b.disclosed: Rail disclosures expose existing period navigator, inclusion and summary routes; task details and scoped options retain all actions.
b.access: 44px nonoverlapping segments that wrap; visible focus; native buttons and descriptive labels.
b.benefit: Offers a stable path to context changes without cycling through many badges.
b.risk: Breadcrumb styling can falsely suggest navigation hierarchy.
b.verification: Check each segment's behavior, selected historical period, section override scope and 320px wrapping.

a.title: High-contrast command bands
a.mechanism: Adversarially assume low vision makes translucent controls disappear: use opaque command bands for page and section actions, with one high-contrast summary control; task rows use a strong completion outline and labelled details.
a.visible: Period, headings, completion state and obvious action bands.
a.disclosed: Summary opens scope/estimates/status; task details retains all editable facts and links; section commands retain existing menus.
a.access: 44px targets, non-color state text, visible focus and no blur beneath text; contrast tested in both themes.
a.benefit: Makes interactions identifiable without scattering colored badges.
a.risk: Bands can visually compete if every section is expanded.
a.verification: Check contrast, forced colors, all routine status states, mobile wrapping and untouched business calculations.

b.title: Return-to-work checkpoint
b.mechanism: An adversarial action view for missed periods places a compact checkpoint before Start: selected historical/current period and own-versus-accumulated scope remain explicit. Sections have scoped checkpoints; tasks retain immediate completion and visible period exceptions.
b.visible: Checkpoint, title, counts, scope and task completion.
b.disclosed: Checkpoint opens existing navigator, diagnostics, accumulated setting and estimates; Start calls original callback; Details and Options preserve all remaining actions. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px controls, explicit date labels, focus management and unchanged completion semantics.
b.benefit: Returning users can understand what they are about to act on.
b.risk: Extra checkpoint may feel repetitive across sections.
b.verification: Verify missed periods, partial targets, selected dates, scope callback independence and 320px.

a.title: Persistent scope watermark
a.mechanism: The planner's adversarial hierarchy treats mistaken accumulated scope as the main hazard. A restrained textual scope watermark sits underneath the page title and every section whose scope differs; other metadata stays quiet.
a.visible: Selected month, explicit own/combined scope text, titles and completion.
a.disclosed: Watermark opens scope toggle with current state plus duration and diagnostic; task Details opens original metadata; list/section Options remains visible. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px watermark button, text rather than color signal, semantic state and keyboard access.
a.benefit: Scope survives even when supporting controls are disclosed.
a.risk: Too many differing scopes can repeat context.
a.verification: Verify section/global independence, own-done/accumulated-pending state, menus, dates and small widths.

b.title: Details-on-demand row expansion
b.mechanism: From first principles, inspecting a reminder should reveal its facts next to its name. TaskCard gains an explicit Detalles expander; page and section summaries use the same inline disclosure grammar without changing task completion.
b.visible: Completion, title, due date and disclosure chevron with text.
b.disclosed: Expanded row exposes duration, price, frequency, day-part and links; page/section expansions retain scope, diagnostics, period navigation and options.
b.access: 44px separate expander, aria-expanded, semantic property buttons and visible focus; no automatic collapse on blur.
b.benefit: Keeps attention anchored to the selected reminder.
b.risk: Many expanded rows can create clutter again.
b.verification: Open two nested task details, edit duration and frequency, collapse safely and verify virtualized heights on mobile.

a.title: Flat inspector hierarchy
a.mechanism: For minimal users, inversion removes nested cards and ornamental surfaces. Keep the primary list flat; header Summary, section Summary and task Details populate one adjacent inspector on desktop or dialog on mobile, always displaying object name.
a.visible: Titles/checks, period, inclusion state, count and clear inspect triggers.
a.disclosed: Inspector includes original estimate/breakdown, routine diagnostic, metadata editors and object options; action groups state page/section/task scope explicitly.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: One secondary surface absorbs complexity without ambiguous unlabeled icons.
a.risk: Selection context may become stale when tasks are removed.
a.verification: Test inspector scope after navigation, deletion, completion and mobile focus restoration.

b.title: Parallel footnote drawer
b.mechanism: For parallel-task planning, first principles keeps active execution on the list and supplementary concurrent duration in a clearly labeled footnote. Header and sections show Active estimate; a Parallel detail button summarizes additional work; tasks show a small parallel text marker.
b.visible: Task completion/title, active estimate, Parallel indicator, date and scope.
b.disclosed: Parallel drawer lists existing parallel breakdown by page, section or task; metadata editors, routine inclusion, diagnostic and all options remain accessible through named controls.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Reduces competition while preserving the meaning of concurrent work.
b.risk: Footnotes may make parallel effort too easy to overlook.
b.verification: Ensure marker remains present for parallel-only tasks and each drawer has explicit object scope.

a.title: Exception gutter
a.mechanism: A caregiver's adversarial hierarchy treats hidden overdue context as a failure. Keep a narrow textual exception gutter for out-of-period dates, accumulated origin and urgent expiry; normal metadata moves into task Details. Headers show selected period and plain summaries; section options remain visible.
a.visible: Titles, completion, selected period and explicit exceptional context.
a.disclosed: Details reveal duration, frequency, price, links and time-of-day; header summaries open existing diagnostics and scope controls. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
a.access: 44px named buttons and focus rings; exception text is never color-only.
a.benefit: Quiet everyday rows while retaining consequential differences.
a.risk: Too many exceptional tasks can refill the gutter.
a.verification: Test overdue, historical, partial and all-done states, metadata callbacks and mobile wrapping.

b.title: Dual context receipt
b.mechanism: A constrained budget context design shows two plain receipt lines: current cost state and temporal/routine scope. Header carries total; sections carry subtotal; tasks keep one price summary and completion, with glass reserved for navigation.
b.visible: Pending euros, selected period/scope, titles and completion.
b.disclosed: Receipt line opens pending/paid split and existing duration where applicable; Details retains full task data and edit callbacks; Options retains every command. Preserve all existing data and callback semantics.
b.access: 44px summary buttons, readable matte text and no color-only cost status.
b.benefit: Separates money from time without a field of badges.
b.risk: Dual summaries still add height in nonshopping views.
b.verification: Verify price/subtask calculations, nonshopping duration, include modes, historical period and 320px.

a.title: User-pinned context fields
a.mechanism: For users needing reminders, inversion rejects a universal assumption about essential metadata. A visible Context display control lets users pin date, recurrence or duration; header/section summarize chosen fields without changing task membership.
a.visible: Pinned fields, title/check, current period, accumulated state and Details.
a.disclosed: Every unpinned field stays in Details; original menus, inclusion, diagnostics and metadata actions remain available regardless of presentation preference.
a.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
a.benefit: Personal emphasis can keep personally meaningful reminders visible.
a.risk: Persistence needs clear per-list or global scope.
a.verification: Verify display preferences never modify tasks, duration visibility policy or historical reference dates.

b.title: Ledger with single material toolbar
b.mechanism: For dense users under constraints, put all summaries into one flat ledger: page total line, section subtotal line, task detail line. Reserve restrained glass for the top command toolbar; use dividers and tabular numbers for density.
b.visible: Dates, count, duration and price in labeled aligned ledger fields.
b.disclosed: Field buttons reveal original editors and source breakdowns; scope selector, routine diagnostic and full menus remain in toolbar/section controls; supplemental metadata expands beneath task.
b.access: Use semantic buttons, 44px nonoverlapping targets, visible focus, keyboard disclosure, scope-specific names and focus return; disable scoped motion when requested.
b.benefit: Keeps substantial information visible without visual surface inflation.
b.risk: Many fields may require responsive column priorities.
b.verification: Check 320px field stacking, shopping exceptions, parallel versus active totals and focus targets.
